knowledge:
- key_parameters: assay=specifies the assay name in the SingleCellExperiment containing raw counts (typically "counts") ;; sorted=logical indicating whether to sort genes by descending deviance in devianceFeatureSelection ;; type=specifies the residual type ("deviance" or "pearson") in nullResiduals ;; L=the number of latent dimensions to fit in GLMPCA (e.g., 2 for visualization, up to 10 for better cluster resolution)
- alternatives: Standard PCA (linear-Gaussian) is not well-suited for small counts; GLM-PCA is more accurate but slower, while Null Residuals (deviance or Pearson) followed by standard PCA is a fast approximation for large datasets. Sparse in-memory Matrix format is faster than HDF5Array/DelayedArray when the dataset fits in memory and is mostly zeros.
- when_to_use: When performing feature selection and dimensionality reduction on single-cell RNA-seq or other count-based transcriptomics datasets where standard linear-Gaussian assumptions do not hold.
- pitfalls: GLM-PCA can be computationally slow for large datasets; use the null residuals approximation instead. Disk-based HDF5Array/DelayedArray data saves memory but significantly slows down computation compared to sparse in-memory Matrix objects.

workflows.name: sce_deviance_glmpca
workflows.intent: Perform deviance-based feature selection and GLM-PCA dimension reduction on a SingleCellExperiment object.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing raw UMI counts in the "counts" assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Rank genes based on binomial deviance using devianceFeatureSelection ;; 2. Subset the SingleCellExperiment to keep only high-deviance genes ;; 3. Run GLM-PCA to reduce dimensionality ;; 4. Extract latent factors from metadata for visualization
workflows.code:
sce<-devianceFeatureSelection(sce, assay="counts", sorted=TRUE)
sce2<-sce[1:1000, ]
set.seed(101)
sce2<-GLMPCA(sce2, 2, assay="counts")
fit<-metadata(sce2)$glmpca
pd<-cbind(as.data.frame(colData(sce2)), fit$factors)

workflows.name: sce_null_residuals_pca
workflows.intent: Perform fast dimension reduction approximation by computing null residuals and running standard PCA.
input: sce (SingleCellExperiment object containing raw UMI counts in the "counts" assay)
workflows.stages: 1. Compute deviance and Pearson null residuals using nullResiduals ;; 2. Subset the SingleCellExperiment to high-deviance genes ;; 3. Run standard PCA on the computed residuals
workflows.code:
sce<-nullResiduals(sce, assay="counts", type="deviance")
sce<-nullResiduals(sce, assay="counts", type="pearson")
sce2<-sce[1:1000, ]
pca<-function(Y, L=2, center=TRUE, scale=TRUE){
    res<-prcomp(as.matrix(t(Y)), center=center, scale.=scale, rank.=L)
    factors<-as.data.frame(res$x)
    colnames(factors)<-paste0("dim", 1:L)
    factors
}
pca_d<-pca(assay(sce2, "binomial_deviance_residuals"))
pca_d$resid_type<-"deviance_residuals"
pca_p<-pca(assay(sce2, "binomial_pearson_residuals"))
pca_p$resid_type<-"pearson_residuals"

workflows.name: large_data_deviance
workflows.intent: Calculate deviance feature selection and null residuals on large, disk-backed (HDF5/DelayedArray) or sparse in-memory matrices.
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out unexpressed genes from the HDF5/DelayedArray counts ;; 2. Run devianceFeatureSelection directly on the HDF5/DelayedArray counts ;; 3. Run nullResiduals on the HDF5-backed SingleCellExperiment
